checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and pull all encounters in that window: ED visits, urgent care, hospital admissions, and observation stays, with discharge summaries and reasons.

Ischemic heart disease (onset 2026-06-30): review chest pain or anginal episodes, nitroglycerin spray use frequency, and any cardiology visits, testing, or procedures since the last review. Flag any new exertional symptoms, dyspnea, or syncope for team discussion.

Medication reconciliation: verify that metoprolol succinate, clopidogrel, simvastatin, nitroglycerin spray, and alendronic acid are still active and taken as prescribed. Note any starts, stops, dose changes, or missed refills in the window. Flag for team discussion any bleeding or bruising reports on clopidogrel, and any heart rate or dizziness concerns on metoprolol.

Alendronic acid and osteoporosis (onset 2023-06-13): check adherence to the dosing schedule, GI symptoms or dysphagia, dental status, and any fractures, falls, or new back pain. Confirm bone density follow-up or calcium/vitamin D status is documented if the team tracks it.

Falls and fracture risk: count falls and near-falls in the window, injuries, and fall-risk screening results. Relevant given osteoporosis, scoliosis, chronic pain, and new cardiac medications that may affect blood pressure.

Chronic pain and chronic intractable migraine: review pain scores, migraine frequency and days per month, acute medication use including any opioid or triptan use, and any new pain-related prescriptions or referrals.

Substance use (dependent drug abuse, onset 2018-06-19): review any documented use, relapse, withdrawal, or counseling and treatment engagement in the window. Check prescriptions for controlled substances and any early refill or pharmacy pattern concerns. Handle sensitively and confirm consent and disclosure limits before sharing in the IDT.
Weight and BMI trend (obesity, BMI 30+): record weights across the window and compare with the prior review. Note any unintended loss or gain and any dietary or activity referrals.
Blood pressure and heart rate: pull all readings in the window, note trends and any hypotension or bradycardia, especially after the metoprolol start on 2026-07-07.

Function, ADLs/IADLs, and cognition: compare current ADL and IADL status with the prior review, including mobility and transfers. Review any cognitive screening, mood screening (for example PHQ), and attendance at PACE day services, transportation issues, and missed appointments. Also check the dental issue (impacted molars) for pain, infection, or pending extraction or referral, since it may affect nutrition and pain.

trace.headline: Jerónimo had a fall on 2026-09-25 and has new evening confusion since late October, including a stove left on. His grandson and primary caregiver Robert reported exhaustion and asked for respite on 2026-11-22.

items.statement: On 2026-11-02 Robert reported about two weeks of increased evening confusion, with the stove left on once. Jerónimo was oriented to person and place but not date, with no fever. The nurse planned a urinalysis, medication review and PCP visit that week. The notes provided do not show results or the outcome of that plan.

On 2026-09-25 Jerónimo fell getting out of bed at home and was found on the floor by his grandson. He denied head strike or loss of consciousness and had a small left forearm skin tear. Fall risk was reassessed as high and a PT referral was placed. On 2026-09-29 PT found his gait slow and unsteady with intermittent cane use and a Timed Up and Go of 19 seconds. PT recommended a front-wheeled walker, a home safety evaluation and bathroom grab bars, and will see him twice weekly.

On 2026-11-22 Robert, the primary caregiver, reported exhaustion and poor sleep. He is worried about managing evenings alone and requested respite. Respite options and a caregiver support group were discussed.
No influenza vaccine is recorded for the current season, which began 2026-08-01. The most recent dose on record was 2026-06-30.

results.reason: The note supports the confusion, stove, orientation, no fever and plan. But the statement says 'Robert reported... Jerónimo was oriented' fine. The added claim that the notes do not show results is an accurate absence statement. However the note does not say 'the nurse planned'; it was a nurse note, which is fine. Minor: the statement is essentially fully supported, but I rate partial because 'evening confusion' is accurate and nothing is contradicted... see below.
